Please solve this issue:

## Bug Description

Two problems have been detected in the DHCP client code:

1. The DHCPREQUEST message does not contain the same 'xid' as the DHCPOFFER message. According to RFC 2131 (page 38 and table 5): 'The DHCPREQUEST message contains the same xid as the DHCPOFFER message.' In the current implementation, each time a DHCPREQUEST is sent, the xid value is incremented, so the xid of the DHCPREQUEST differs from the DHCPOFFER.

2. The PAD option is not processed correctly. According to RFC 2132 (page 4): 'Options may be fixed length or variable length. All options begin with a tag octet. Fixed-length options without data consist of only a tag octet. Only options 0 and 255 are fixed length. All other options are variable-length with a length octet following the tag octet.' In the current implementation, option 0 (PAD option) is processed as a variable-length option, so when present, an extra byte is read as the option length and corrupts option processing.

Impact: Some DHCP servers discard DHCPREQUEST messages because the xid value differs from the DHCPOFFER. Additionally, incorrect PAD option processing can cause out-of-buffer readings and assertion failures on malformed messages.

The bugs are in subsys/net/lib/dhcpv4/dhcpv4.c and subsys/net/lib/dhcpv4/dhcpv4_internal.h.
